integratedBehavior: The JSON Schema 2020-12 core model distinguishes canonical aggregate and immutable revision identity, observed and canonical labels, disputed alternatives, partial dates, rights, confidence, status, source references, provenance and typed scholarly aggregates. Generated Python and TypeScript reject UUIDv4 identities, path-bearing source references, malformed or non-finite values, false canonical certainty, and mutation of frozen results.

The lifecycle catalog defines deterministic commands, actor/reason requirements, emitted facts, optimistic revisions, terminal states and explicit reopen rules for projects, corpus items, documents, evidence records, decisions, tasks, dossiers and exports. Both runtimes deny illegal, stale, malformed, maximum-revision and unsafe-integer transitions before returning a persistable transition.

The compatibility policy freezes current and prior releases, additive/deprecation/breaking rules, exact highest-common negotiation, accepted ADR and reader-bridge authority, and a supported event catalog. Unknown types and unsupported versions deny after exactly one immutable content-free audit callback; unknown payload fields deny before dispatch; audit failure remains fail closed.

Governed textual authority uses canonical UTF-8 LF hashing so Windows Git checkout conversion cannot fabricate drift, while the migration fixture remains raw-byte-bound. Generation and runtime outputs stay deterministic across branch checkout and process restart without ambient filesystem reads during assessment.

The Core service and real frozen sidecar consume the generated modules through stable portable interfaces. The slice introduces no persistence schema, renderer route, external provider, hosted infrastructure, secret, network egress, or user-facing experience change.
